question.text: Under NSE equity derivatives, what does the 'lot size' (contract size) of an option contract mean?

answer.text: The lot size is defined by the exchange and can change; it specifies the number of units per contract
100 shares per contract for all options
The lot size is decided by the option buyer at the time of purchase

explanation.text: The Logic: Each option contract has a fixed lot size (contract size) that specifies the number of units of the underlying per contract. The contract size is determined by the exchange and can be revised periodically. The contract value = premium x lot size. The Trap: Lot size is not chosen by the trader. It is standardised by the exchange and can be changed by the exchange from time to time. Note: For example, if Nifty options have a lot size of 50, one contract represents 50 units of the Nifty index for pricing and settlement purposes.
